question: Among one-layer Transformers that both reach 100% test accuracy on modular addition at the same global weight norm, does selecting a high-Boltzmann-entropy equilibrium state improve retention when the network is subsequently trained to memorize 500 new examples, and is that retention associated with broader weight spectra?

key_findings.claim: Perfect grokking does not determine retention: the WLMD-selected equilibrium checkpoint preserves much more original-task test accuracy than the AdamW checkpoint after both fit the same new random examples.
key_findings.evidence: Both models exceed 99.8% accuracy on the mixed original-plus-new training set while retaining 100% accuracy on the original training examples. Under random inputs with newly mapped labels, original held-out accuracy falls from 100% to about 75% for AdamW but remains about 95% for WLMD across ten noise-training seeds.

anchors.section: Noise Injection Protocol and Experimental Results

key_findings.claim: The retention gap shrinks monotonically as the added rule becomes more structurally similar to the original modular-addition task.
key_findings.evidence: After learning x^2+y mod 37, original test accuracy is approximately 84% for AdamW and above 98% for WLMD. After learning x+y mod 37, it is approximately 97% and 100%, respectively, compared with roughly 75% and 95% under random inputs.

key_findings.claim: The higher-retention state is also less plastic under the paper's stopping protocol.
key_findings.evidence: WLMD checkpoints consistently require more fine-tuning epochs than AdamW checkpoints to exceed 99.8% combined training accuracy for all three added-data types. Thus the result is a stability-plasticity tradeoff, not an unqualified improvement in adaptation.

key_findings.claim: WLMD checkpoints begin with dramatically broader attention and MLP singular-value spectra and retain higher effective rank in those core matrices after random-example training.
key_findings.evidence: Before injection, effective ranks for W_Q, W_K, W_in, and W_out are 96.8, 97.4, 116.1, and 116.6 for WLMD versus 2.2, 7.2, 48.1, and 33.7 for AdamW. WLMD loses more rank during adaptation but still ends at 68.3, 86.7, 83.1, and 100.4 versus 2.4, 6.9, 41.4, and 44.6; the unembedding is an exception, ending lower for WLMD.

key_findings.claim: Retention is not explained by simply moving less far in parameter space.
key_findings.evidence: For most attention and MLP matrices, the WLMD pre/post cosine similarity is lower than AdamW's—for example 0.8383 versus 0.9964 for W_Q and 0.8566 versus 0.9960 for W_in—yet WLMD retains the old function better. The authors interpret this as room to move inside a larger basin, though no basin-boundary intervention tests that mechanism.

key_findings.claim: The effective-rank explanation is correlational, not causal.
key_findings.evidence: The study compares two training or sampling procedures that simultaneously change entropy, spectra, loss, and optimization history. The authors explicitly call for interventions that directly manipulate effective rank to determine whether it causes robustness or merely correlates with it.

key_findings.claim: The central comparison is not a test-label-free optimizer comparison: test accuracy is one coordinate of the sampled entropy landscape and is used to select the equilibrium checkpoint.
key_findings.evidence: WLMD estimates S(L_train,A_test)=log V(L_train,A_test) for 1.2e8 epochs, then the authors select a state on the converged equilibrium curve with A_test=100% and log training loss near -1. AdamW is trained for 120 epochs to A_test=100% and log training loss near -2.

method.core_idea: Hold original test accuracy and global weight norm fixed, contrast a conventional grokked solution with a high-volume equilibrium state sampled from a Boltzmann entropy landscape, then measure how much held-out knowledge survives supervised adaptation to new inputs.
method.mechanism: Train a roughly 215K-parameter one-layer, four-head Transformer on 2,244 examples of x+y mod 67. Produce one checkpoint with full-batch AdamW and global norm projection to ||w||=30. Separately run Wang-Landau Molecular Dynamics for 1.2e8 epochs over the joint landscape of log training loss and test accuracy at the same norm, and select a maximum-entropy checkpoint with 100% test accuracy. Double embedding and output vocabulary size, introduce 500 examples from random inputs, x^2+y mod 37, or x+y mod 37, and fine-tune each checkpoint on those examples plus the original training set with AdamW until combined accuracy exceeds 99.8%. Across ten new-data seeds, track original held-out accuracy, epochs to fit, layerwise effective rank computed from normalized singular values, and pre/post parameter cosine similarity.
assumptions: A state selected from S(L_train,A_test) at perfect test accuracy is a meaningful model of true thermodynamic equilibrium rather than a test-conditioned research instrument.
Global norm projection to 30 adequately controls scale-related differences between training procedures.
The AdamW and WLMD checkpoints are sufficiently matched even though their log training losses are approximately -2 and -1, respectively.
Ten fine-tuning seeds applied to one checkpoint per pretraining procedure characterize procedure-level robustness.
Retaining original held-out accuracy while original training examples remain in every update is a valid measure of catastrophic forgetting.
The three added datasets form an ordered spectrum of task similarity, although two are coherent arithmetic tasks rather than label noise.
Entropy of parameter-space volume at a fixed global norm is comparable across these checkpoints and relevant to functional robustness.
Entropy of the normalized singular values—not squared singular values—is an informative measure of representational richness.

techniques.role: Samples log parameter-space volume jointly over training loss and test accuracy instead of following a loss gradient to one solution.
Projects both procedures to norm 30 to remove one major grokking and scale confound.
Adds new examples only after both checkpoints reach perfect original test accuracy, exposing hidden differences in retention.
Keeps all 2,244 original training examples in every adaptation run so lost held-out accuracy cannot be attributed to complete absence of old data.
Varies the new mapping from random inputs to a different polynomial rule to the same addition rule under a new modulus.
Summarizes how evenly each weight matrix uses its singular directions before and after interference.
Uses pre/post cosine similarity to test whether robustness is merely a consequence of smaller parameter movement.
Duplicates embeddings and output projections so new symbols occupy distinct token indices while preserving the original input-output interface.

evaluations.setting: Original x+y mod 67 model adapted to 500 random-input examples, ten seeds
evaluations.metric: Original held-out accuracy after combined training accuracy exceeds 99.8%
evaluations.result: WLMD retains about 95% while fixed-norm AdamW falls to about 75%
evaluations.baseline: AdamW-goldilocks checkpoint with the same norm 30 and initial 100% original test accuracy

evaluations.metric: Original held-out accuracy at the same memorization threshold
evaluations.result: WLMD remains above 98% while AdamW is about 84%
evaluations.baseline: The same two checkpoint types under structured but nonmatching arithmetic

evaluations.metric: Original held-out accuracy at the same memorization threshold
evaluations.result: WLMD is about 100% and AdamW about 97%, the smallest gap
evaluations.baseline: The same two checkpoint types under a closely related modular-addition rule

evaluations.metric: Epochs required to exceed 99.8% mixed-set training accuracy
evaluations.result: WLMD consistently takes longer, revealing reduced plasticity alongside stronger retention

evaluations.metric: Pre/post effective rank and parameter cosine similarity
evaluations.result: WLMD starts and ends much higher-rank in all attention and MLP matrices despite larger rank loss and usually larger parameter displacement; its unembedding ends lower-rank than AdamW's
evaluations.baseline: The corresponding matrices of the AdamW-goldilocks checkpoint

limitations: Author-stated: the empirical setting is one shallow Transformer on modular arithmetic; NLP, images, deeper networks, LLMs, and model-size scaling remain untested.
Author-stated: effective rank is correlational evidence, and causal relations among entropy, rank, and retention are unresolved.
Author-stated: WLMD is not a practical training method at this scale, while the proposed WanD direction remains unstable.

Reviewer-identified: WLMD explicitly samples entropy as a function of test accuracy and the selected checkpoint is conditioned on 100% test performance, creating test-label leakage that prevents a deployable optimizer comparison.
Reviewer-identified: WLMD uses 1.2e8 epochs versus 120 AdamW pretraining epochs, so the procedures differ by roughly six orders of magnitude in nominal iteration count before adaptation.

Reviewer-identified: the starting log training losses are about -1 for WLMD and -2 for AdamW, contrary to the paper's repeated description of similar or controlled loss; a factor-e loss difference can affect margin and retention.
Reviewer-identified: only one pretrained checkpoint per procedure is used; the ten seeds resample adaptation, not independent WLMD landscapes or AdamW pretraining runs.
Reviewer-identified: old training data are replayed in full during adaptation, so this is interference in held-out generalization rather than the common no-replay continual-learning protocol.
Reviewer-identified: x^2+y mod 37 and x+y mod 37 are new structured tasks, not random-label noise, and should not be aggregated under a single noise label.
Reviewer-identified: vocabulary doubling, duplicated old rows, randomly initialized new rows, and 31 unused token indices may interact differently with checkpoints having radically different spectra.

Reviewer-identified: the paper promises AdamW-standard, AdamW-full, infrastructure, dependency, hyperparameter, and spectrum results in an appendix, but the extracted nine-page manuscript ends with references and contains no appendix.
Reviewer-identified: no established continual-learning baselines such as EWC, SI, or replay variants are evaluated despite being discussed.
Reviewer-identified: post-injection rank is not uniformly higher for WLMD—the unembedding reverses—so a single rank-buffer story does not cover every layer.
Reviewer-identified: there are no functional circuit analyses or interventions establishing that the high-rank directions encode redundant copies of the original algorithm.
failure_modes: A test-conditioned entropy sampler may select checkpoints that look robust only because held-out labels participated in state selection.
WLMD's retention advantage may partly reflect its higher starting loss or smaller margins rather than entropy alone.
High stability can simply make a model slower to learn new data, producing an unfavorable stability-plasticity tradeoff in a stream with rapid task changes.
The result may disappear across independent equilibrium and AdamW checkpoints if the observed pair is atypical.
A wider singular spectrum can encode nuisance directions rather than redundant task structure, so increasing effective rank directly may not improve retention.
Global norm projection can hide layerwise scale differences that drive both effective rank and optimizer sensitivity.
Vocabulary expansion may force interference through shared hidden layers in a way that does not resemble continual learning with a fixed output space.
Full replay of old training samples can preserve interpolation while the learned extrapolating circuit is replaced, exactly the behavior measured here but not necessarily ordinary forgetting.
At larger depth or parameter count, full entropy-landscape sampling becomes computationally intractable and may not mix to equilibrium.
When the new task is sufficiently similar, the retention metric saturates near 100% and cannot distinguish procedures.
reusable_insights: After matching endpoint accuracy, probe how a representation behaves under subsequent learning; static generalization can hide large differences in stability.
Report adaptation speed and retention together so robustness is not confused with simple resistance to updating.
Use a graded family of new tasks to estimate how representational overlap mediates interference.
Audit spectral metrics layer by layer; a global high-rank narrative can conceal exceptions such as the unembedding reversal.
Parameter displacement and functional forgetting are distinct: a model can move farther yet retain more if its solution region is broad.
Match training loss, margins, norm, compute, and checkpoint-selection information—not only test accuracy—before attributing robustness to landscape volume.
Intervene on a proposed mediator such as effective rank rather than treating correlation between two optimizer-produced checkpoints as mechanism.
Separate replay-based held-out generalization loss from no-replay catastrophic forgetting in continual-learning terminology.
open_questions: Does the retention gap persist when entropy-state selection never observes test labels and checkpoints are matched tightly on training loss and margin?
What happens across multiple independent WLMD and AdamW pretraining seeds rather than multiple adaptation seeds from one checkpoint each?
Can a practical optimizer approximate the high-volume state without 1.2e8 WLMD epochs or unstable WanD dynamics?
Does directly increasing attention or MLP effective rank improve retention, or is rank only a byproduct of entropy sampling?
Which singular directions encode the modular-addition circuit, and which directions are actually overwritten by each new task?
How does the method compare with EWC, Synaptic Intelligence, replay subsampling, parameter isolation, or flat-minima continual-learning methods under equal compute?
Does high entropy help in class-incremental and task-incremental settings without full access to old training data?
How do retention and plasticity scale with model depth, width, data complexity, and the number of sequential tasks?
Would function-space entropy or local posterior volume predict retention more robustly than parameter-space volume under reparameterization?
Are the missing standard/full-AdamW and spectrum appendices consistent with the paper's central controlled comparison?

competitive_landscape.title: High-entropy Advantage in Neural Networks' Generalizability
competitive_landscape.difference: Yang et al. introduce the same Wang-Landau entropy-landscape program and report that high-volume states generalize better across arithmetic, tabular, image, and language tasks up to roughly one million parameters. The Grokked Illusion does not originate high-entropy sampling; it narrows to one modular-arithmetic model and adds a post-learning retention test while controlling initial test accuracy.

competitive_landscape.title: Is Grokking a Computational Glass Relaxation?
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhang et al. already map modular-arithmetic grokking to a glass-relaxation process, construct its entropy landscape, identify an especially large high-entropy generalization advantage, and propose the WanD toy optimizer. The current paper reuses that exact controlled regime and contributes the new interference experiment plus spectral correlates, not the equilibrium account of grokking itself.

competitive_landscape.title: Entropy-SGD: Biasing Gradient Descent Into Wide Valleys
competitive_landscape.difference: Chaudhari et al. optimize a differentiable local-entropy objective with nested Langevin dynamics and evaluate generalization in convolutional and recurrent networks. The Grokked Illusion estimates a global Boltzmann volume over training loss and test accuracy with vastly more expensive WLMD, then evaluates retention; it offers no practical optimizer or direct Entropy-SGD baseline.

competitive_landscape.title: Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting in Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Kirkpatrick et al.'s Elastic Weight Consolidation explicitly slows changes to parameters important for old tasks and demonstrates sequential retention on MNIST and Atari without needing an equilibrium sampler. The Grokked Illusion studies whether the initial solution geometry is intrinsically resistant while all old training samples remain available; it diagnoses a property but does not compare against or replace an established mitigation algorithm.

competitive_landscape.title: Continual Learning Through Synaptic Intelligence
competitive_landscape.difference: Zenke et al. accumulate online per-synapse importance and regularize later learning, explicitly optimizing the stability-plasticity balance in sequential classification. The current paper instead compares one preselected high-entropy checkpoint with one AdamW checkpoint and observes that the more stable state learns the new examples more slowly, leaving the practical balance unresolved.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: the paper discovers the 'grokked illusion'—two models with saturated original generalization can have very different retention—and extends the high-entropy advantage from generalization to robustness, with high effective rank proposed as a buffer against interference. Reviewer inference: high-entropy optimization, entropy landscapes, high-entropy grokking, and catastrophic-forgetting mitigation all have substantial prior art, including two directly preceding papers from the same research line. The defensible novelty is the compact experiment that equal endpoint test accuracy does not imply equal post-adaptation retention, together with a layerwise spectral and displacement audit. The mechanistic claim must be narrowed to association: test labels participate in WLMD selection, starting losses and compute are not matched, only one pretrained checkpoint per procedure is tested, and rank is never manipulated causally.
reviewer_notes: All nine extracted pages were checked end to end. Pages 8-9 are references; despite repeated cross-references, the manuscript contains no appendix, which is a material reporting contradiction because the standard/full-AdamW controls and infrastructure details are said to reside there. Numeric retention and effective-rank values were taken from Figure 1 and Table 1. Competitive records were verified against primary arXiv or OpenReview sources current through 2026-08-23.
